## The problem: using context

In “The cat chased the dog because it was fast,” the pronoun **it** could refer to either the cat or the dog. A model therefore cannot always interpret a token from its local representation alone: it needs to use information carried by other positions in the sequence.

That is what self-attention provides. For each position, the mechanism builds two things: **where to look** in the context and **what information to bring back**. Q, K, and V provide the representations needed for these two operations.

For the current token in “What have the Romans ever done for us?”, Q is compared with the K vectors at accessible positions; the resulting weights are then used to aggregate their V vectors. This describes the computation, not conscious search or human-like interpretation of the sentence.

This example is adapted from [Neha KK](https://medium.com/@nkk18072004/understanding-queries-keys-and-values-in-transformers-149ed07c9f8b). It motivates the need for context; it does not prove that one isolated head resolves coreference or describe the attention weights of a trained model.

## Three complementary roles

The three projections are easiest to distinguish by following the flow of information:

- **Q — the query:** what the current position is looking to match in the context;
- **K — the key:** what each position presents for comparison with a query;
- **V — the value:** the information carried by that position and available to be transmitted.

Q and K therefore determine **how attention is distributed**. V supplies **the content that is aggregated** using that distribution. K and V can represent different features: compatibility supports routing, while the value carries the transmitted content. They are learned numerical vectors, not readable labels or ready-made answers.

The diagram reveals two paths: one determines the weighting, the other supplies the content. **Why are three distinct projections needed to build these two paths from the same input?**

## Why three projections from the same input?

In self-attention, Q, K, and V are three learned transformations of the same representation stream. $X$ denotes the input to the attention sublayer: in the first block it starts from token embeddings; in later blocks it is an already contextualized hidden state. Positional information may be added upstream ([positional embeddings](positional-encoding.qmd)) or incorporated into queries and keys, as with [RoPE](rope.qmd).

For a sequence of $T$ positions, write $X\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times d_{model}}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
Q &= XW_Q,\\
K &= XW_K,\\
V &= XW_V.
\end{aligned}
$$

The matrices $W_Q$, $W_K$, and $W_V$ are **distinct but learned jointly**. They let the model build, from the same input, representations suited to two different functions: computing compatibility (Q and K) and carrying content (V). This parameterization follows [Vaswani et al. (2017), *Attention Is All You Need*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762). For a complementary visual introduction, see [How Query, Key, and Value (QKV) Work in Transformers](https://dev.to/nishanthan-k/how-query-key-and-value-qkv-work-in-transformers-199a); the equations, dimensions, and interpretive limits are established in this lesson and the [advanced Q/K/V deep dive](queries-keys-values-advanced.qmd).

With $W_Q,W_K\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{model}\times d_k}$ and $W_V\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{model}\times d_v}$, the outputs have these shapes:

- $Q,K\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times d_k}$;
- $V\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times d_v}$.

Each row corresponds to one position. The same projection matrices are applied at every position, while the input representations vary. The dimensions $d_k$ and $d_v$ need not be equal; optional biases are omitted here. This shared provenance is specific to self-attention; in [cross-attention](cross-attention.qmd), Q comes from the querying stream, while K and V come from the stream being queried. To trace these projections in the block implementation, see the [guided Transformer-block walkthrough](transformer-block-walkthrough.qmd); general dimension and axis conventions are covered in the [tensor reference](tensors.qmd).

## Mathematical and architectural deep dive

Per-position equations, compatibility geometry, gradient paths, and multi-head variants become useful once the mental model is established. They are collected in the [advanced Q/K/V deep dive](queries-keys-values-advanced.qmd), rather than scattered across several collapsed callouts on this page.

## Takeaway and next steps

The functional distinction is simple but fundamental:

- **Q and K** determine compatibility scores, then attention weights;
- **V** supplies the vectors combined using those weights;
- changing V alone therefore leaves the weights unchanged, even though the aggregated content may change.

The weights are not a universal measure of semantic relevance, and attention is not nearest-neighbour search in the initial embedding space: it operates on learned projections. The limits of this interpretation and the gradient paths are developed in the [advanced Q/K/V deep dive](queries-keys-values-advanced.qmd).

The next lesson, [Scaled dot-product attention](scaled-dot-product-attention.qmd), explains how scores become weights and how those weights aggregate V.

To practise the skills associated with this lesson, the [Attention exercises](exercises-attention.qmd#attention) cover projection calculations and dimensions, predicting the effects of changing $W_Q$, $W_K$, or $W_V$, connecting projections to backpropagation, and transferring the reasoning to cross-attention and GQA/MQA. Numerical calculations remain in that practice route.

::: {.callout-note .learning-outcomes collapse="true" title="Learning outcomes"}
By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
- distinguish the roles of Q, K, and V in the attention mechanism;
- explain why Q and K determine the weights while V supplies the aggregated content;
- describe the qualitative dependencies between projections, weights, and content, without performing matrix calculations.
:::

[Dedicated exercises on Q/K/V and attention](exercises/queries-keys-values.qmd).

Which projections determine attention weights, and which one supplies the aggregated content? What happens if V changes while Q and K remain fixed?

<details>
<summary>Show the reasoning</summary>

Q and K determine the scores and therefore the attention weights. V supplies the aggregated vectors. If only V changes, the weights remain the same, but the aggregated result can change.
